passedTitles.title: ✔ normal demo cleanup stops active runs, preserves history and excludes prefix/version lookalikes
✔ committed messages push addresses, notification receipts preserve read and ACK semantics
✔ stopped, terminal, expired, disabled and cross-owner runs never receive notifications
✔ real Postgres: idle gateway presence drives dispatch, device selection and post-commit uninstall
✔ owner revoke stops attributed work, revokes worker access, records once and preserves sibling credentials
✔ a receipt write fault rolls token, stop, lease and worker revocation back atomically
✔ a revocation waits for the admitted writer transaction, and later raw/ORM admissions all refuse
✔ the actual event route accepts before revoke and rejects the old token after a fresh request scope
✔ revocation while the real event handler waits for its body prevents the later write
✔ terminating an admitted write connection rolls back both the write and authority lock
✔ a long poll loses token authority within its five-second database polling interval
✔ with push, revocation ends a waiting long poll on its NOTIFY, long before any timer; a lost NOTIFY still fails it at the deadline
✔ existing device removal still refuses live work, then records revocation without deleting history
✔ a device request is fenced by its first statement, with no check up front, and reads no device report it does not use
✔ one read of a device's runs finds its stops, messages and queued runs
✔ the idle check answers in one statement, finds the same work and pending device commands, and refuses a revoked credential
✔ the same credential remains valid for its established heartbeat route
✔ own run renewal passes route authentication and reaches issuance once
✔ another device and another run remain refused before issuance
✔ an ended machine cannot obtain a new lease
✔ revoked cloud credentials remain refused
✔ a bound cloud device can renew its own subscription lease through the actual route
✔ a heartbeat re-checks execution identities only when the harnesses change or the device comes back, and renews the leases of the runs it reports
✔ runs poll reads current authority, ownership and results in one snapshot
✔ repos poll reads current authority, ownership and results in one snapshot
✔ initial claim repository handoff removes a real cloud repos request without increasing SQL, rows or response bytes
✔ every device route refuses a token revoked after authentication before it calls out or issues anything
✔ a revocation waits for the burst in flight; the next burst answers 401
✔ between bursts (a wait, network IO) the fence is not held: a revocation goes through at once
✔ a hung unit loses its fence after 10 s; the revocation then completes and the unit fails closed
✔ when no fence connection can be had the request is refused with 503, never run unfenced
✔ ten concurrent multi-statement device requests complete with three fence connections; fewer authorization transactions and round trips than one fence per statement
✔ desktop account context reads only the current browser owner's active local devices
✔ local setup owner view retains fresh session checks without reading unused devices
✔ owner token pagination preserves microsecond ordering and rejects foreign or malformed anchors
✔ registration grant is user-bound, expires, and has one concurrent winner
✔ registration grant consumption uses one PostgreSQL statement
✔ a failed credential insertion does not consume the enrollment grant
✔ daemon acceptance follows real local enrollment and owner routes without a cloud token binding
✔ online removal offers only uninstall, and its own receipt revokes credentials
✔ unacknowledged uninstall expires after ten minutes; offline removal revokes immediately
✔ management queue is owner-scoped, serial and acknowledges only its device
✔ pending commands without receipts are one read and preserve current device removal state
✔ a fresh login cannot admit an old daemon, and updating cannot revive a revoked credential
✔ registration metadata cannot disguise an old daemon behind a current header

boundaries: All four PostgreSQL service jobs naturally completed success; each final log fetched once. No rerun, cancellation, source modification or new database/model job was performed.
The actual 90e698 merge tree includes late main0e411802. The head548 tree933f is not substituted for it.

C canonical segments actually pass 16+11+5=32 tests. Runs/repos each report 2 PostgreSQL statements; same frozen test blob checks initial real authentication then revoked/expired/removed/foreign-owner params barriers before any business read. These are isolated CI fixtures.
The existing protected two-statement unitFence prototype still exercises ten concurrent requests and strict explicit transaction/round-trip assertions. It is not a production performance benchmark.

The previous c1 standalone baseline probe TimeoutExpired remains a separate failure with no candidate execution. Current success does not reinterpret that failure as assertion RED or a successful old run.
No production result or full Native budget is established by these PG results. The 473/402 original Native RED and conditional fixed-inventory analysis are unchanged.

Raw logs remain local under private pending any publication scan; GitHub masking is not treated as proof of absence of all sensitive data. Full API originals include public Git metadata and are not selected for publication by this report.
